gamete.def: A sex cell with one set of chromosomes: a sperm in males, an oocyte (egg) in females. An oocyte that has finished meiosis is called an ovum.

ploidy.def: A diploid (2n) cell holds both members of every chromosome pair, 46 in humans; a haploid (n) cell holds one of each pair, 23. Homologous chromosomes are the two members of a pair, one from each parent, with the same genes in the same order; the versions of a gene they carry are alleles.

meiosis.def: The division that makes gametes: one round of DNA copying, then two divisions. Meiosis I pairs the homologs, lets them cross over and separates them; meiosis II separates the sister chromatids, giving four haploid cells that all differ. Failure of chromosomes to separate is nondisjunction.

sex-chromosomes.def: The 23rd chromosome pair: XX in a typical female, XY in a typical male. Every egg carries an X and each sperm an X or a Y, so the sperm sets the sex; the SRY gene on the Y turns the early gonad into a testis.
